subject.title: trusted-proxy auth: support fallback/default user when identity header is absent

question: Should trusted-proxy auth support an explicit fallback identity when a request is from a configured trusted proxy but the identity header is absent?
rationale: This is not a narrow bug fix: it changes who OpenClaw authenticates as when the upstream proxy provides no per-user identity, which affects Gateway authorization, Control UI access, session scoping, and operator trust boundaries.

options.title: Keep fail-closed and document unsupported
options.body: Reject missing identity headers in trusted-proxy mode and document Cloudflare IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket deployments as requiring password auth, Tailscale Serve, or a proxy path that forwards identity.

options.title: Accept a narrow opt-in fallback
options.body: Add a named fallback identity only with explicit config, required proxy-owned headers or signed assertions, allowUsers validation, security audit warnings, and regression coverage.

options.title: Defer to a broader auth redesign
options.body: Keep this issue open as canonical input while designing a more general identity-bearing proxy policy instead of adding a one-off fallback key.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed and document unsupported
recommendation.body: Reject missing identity headers in trusted-proxy mode and document Cloudflare IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket deployments as requiring password auth, Tailscale Serve, or a proxy path that forwards identity.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current issue router for this trusted-proxy cluster and have adjacent auth fallback history.
